Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/general/workflow.md

# Writing and correcting Total.js apps

Use this workflow with the [source map](sources.md) and the pages for the affected zone. It is a review method, not an automatic certification.

## Before writing

1. Read the target project's instructions, entry point, dependencies and nearest working feature. Identify the backend version, browser UI major, storage model and route registration pattern.
2. Select a concrete reference: for example CMS redirects for a FileStorage feature, or OpenPlatform groups for SQL CRUD. Read its route, action, screen and form together.
3. Record the contracts you must preserve: URL and action ID, body/query/params, response envelope, permission IDs, settings keys and plugin/model paths.
4. Find the native helper or existing component before creating a wrapper. See [native patterns](native-patterns.md). Read only the component documentation compatible with the app's UI version.

## Write a feature

Implement the same direct flow as the reference: route → validated action → existing storage → one response, with the UI calling that endpoint and binding its result. Keep `exports`, `$`, `model`, `self`, `config`, `cls` and familiar field names. Add only the files the feature needs. Keep business checks in the action; input validation does not establish ownership or authorization.

For SQL-backed features follow [queries](../database/queries.md) and add the schema upgrade if needed. For memory/FileStorage features use the app's existing load/save and cache hooks. For UI changes follow [binding and forms](../frontend/binding-and-forms.md).

## Correct existing code

Review a bounded feature or diff. For each finding record:

| Field | What to record |
|---|---|
| Location | File and line, with the concrete code |
| Rule | Page and reference file that support the finding |
| Kind | Runtime/API defect, contract change, convention mismatch or optional simplification |
| Correction | Smallest change that fixes it and the callers it affects |
| Verification | Observable result that would demonstrate the fix |

Remove duplicated validation and pass-through wrappers when a native call expresses the same behaviour. Keep ownership/business checks, cancellation, error mapping and other behaviour that the native replacement does not supply. Do not replace all storage with SQL, migrate UI versions or split actions merely to satisfy an example in this guide. Correct action/schema separators to `|` by updating registrations and callers together; check generated endpoints and preserve public URL compatibility. URL paths and plugin method paths keep their own separators.

Make corrections by coherent feature, preserving owner changes. A formatting rewrite and an endpoint redesign have different review risks; keep their intent explicit. Do not edit minified vendor assets, bundles or runtime databases as source.

## Organize files during a refactor

Apply the [project structure](project-structure.md) policy: runtime files in recognizable Total.js folders, private runtime inputs under `private/`, and documentation, evaluation material and independent examples under `docs/`. The running application must not depend on `docs/`; development tools can use its fixtures. Consume automatically loaded modules through `MODS`, while preserving standalone-tool imports.

Before deleting an old tree, remove its runtime reader, routes, generators and obsolete checks together. Preserve contracts unless the requested scope explicitly retires them. Retain the current external integration when replacing local artifacts with an external source, and keep its integrity checks. Generated/minified dependencies and historical evidence must not be silently rewritten as part of a folder move.

Check package contents and private-file allowlists, temporary export layouts, migration inputs and documentation links after moving a file. An old layout may still be intentional input to a one-time legacy migration; document that exception instead of changing what the migration reads.

## Verify the result

- Run `node --check` for changed JS; it does not cover inline scripts in HTML, templates or browser APIs.
- Exercise the affected route with valid and invalid input, anonymous and authorized users, and insufficient permissions. For record operations also check a different owner's record and a missing ID.
- Confirm the response shape expected by the caller, not just a successful HTTP status.
- In the browser, open and reopen the screen/form, create/edit/cancel, submit and confirm caller refresh. Check the served asset and console when the UI changes; test release output if compilation/minification matters.
- Use existing project checks and focused regression tests where behaviour warrants them. Record exactly what ran and what could not run, including unavailable DB, credentials or browser access.

Finish with the concrete changes, evidence and remaining limitations. A successful documentation test only validates this reference's structure; it does not prove an app follows every convention or that its runtime works.

## Project instruction snippet

Add this to a consuming project's instructions when adopting this reference:

```text
Follow the Total.js conventions at https://github.com/totaljs-es/conventions.
Read general/sources.md, general/workflow.md and the pages for this change.
Use the nearest compatible Total.js example. Use | between parts of action
and schema names, never / or \. Update registrations and callers together
when correcting names, checking endpoint compatibility. Preserve URLs,
permissions, storage model and UI major version during corrections.
Keep runtime inputs in private/, internal documentation and examples in docs/,
and loaded application module access through MODS. Preserve standalone-tool
imports and update package/test/export paths when moving files.
Report convention findings with file/line, rule, proposed fix and checks run.
```

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/general/native-patterns.md

# Prefer direct native patterns

The reference apps put operations directly in actions and plugin methods, with shared behaviour in `FUNC` or a dedicated integration module. They do not require a service/repository/DTO stack for each feature. Sources: CMS redirects and `definitions/func.js`; OpenPlatform `plugins/setup/schemas/groups.js`; Todomator `schemas/tickets.js`.

## Choose the existing operation

| Need | First choice | Avoid introducing merely for indirection |
|---|---|---|
| Typed request | `input`, `params`, `query`, shared `@Schema` | A second validator for the same type checks |
| Find a cached item | `items.findItem('id', id)` | A one-use lookup service |
| Query SQL | `DATA.read/find/list/insert/modify/remove` | A repository class mirroring the builder |
| Outgoing HTTP | `RESTBuilder` | A fetch/axios wrapper that duplicates existing transport |
| App paths | `PATH.root/public/databases/temp` | Hard-coded machine paths or a new path resolver |
| App files and metadata | Existing `FILESTORAGE`, `MEMORIZE`, `FUNC.load/save` | A new persistence backend for the same data |
| Shared business operation | Existing action or a small `FUNC.name` | Forwarding through several functions without adding behaviour |
| UI state and calls | `PLUGIN`, model paths, `exports.tapi`, components | A second state store or HTTP client |
| UI events | `exec` and plugin methods | Separate event wiring for standard buttons |

These are selection defaults, not a ban on helpers. A helper earns its place by expressing a reused operation or isolating an integration, not by forwarding the same arguments. Keep names and object shapes familiar to the surrounding app.

## Input is already typed; business rules still matter

Adapted from CMS `plugins/redirects/schemas/redirects.js` (the action ID below uses this repo's pipe default):

```js
NEWACTION('Redirects|read', {
	name: 'Read redirect',
	input: '*id',
	permissions: 'redirects,admin',
	action: function($, model) {
		var item = MAIN.db.redirects.findItem('id', model.id);
		if (item)
			$.callback(item);
		else
			$.invalid(404);
	}
});
```

Do not reparse `model.id` or add an alternative success envelope. In a user-owned feature, also constrain the lookup to the owner or tenant using the target app's existing rule. This CMS example is an admin collection, not a complete ownership model for other products.

## Know the execution context

`Total.*`, `DATA`, `NOW` and prototypes are available after framework initialization; browser `SET`/`PLUGIN` APIs belong to the loaded UI library. A standalone Node script must initialize what it needs. Never replace a tool's valid Node import with an unavailable app global.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/general/project-structure.md

# Project structure

A Total.js 5 app is a folder that the framework loads by convention. Put each kind of file where the framework (and the next reader) expects it.

```
index.js            starts the app: require('total5'); F.run(options)
config              settings, one "key : value" per line
package.json        "total5" is the runtime dependency
controllers/        routes: exports.install = function() { ROUTE(...) }
definitions/        auth.js, init.js, func.js, db.js: loaded at start, no exports
modules/            integrations with other systems (cdn, openplatform, tapi...)
plugins/<name>/     a feature: index.js (server), index.html (UI), schemas/, public/
schemas/            actions that are not part of a plugin
views/              layout and pages (HTML with @{...} directives)
public/             browser-accessible static files
private/            internal runtime files and grouped SQL/maintenance assets
docs/               development documentation, evidence and standalone examples
database.sql        the full schema; changes go to dated files next to it
```

Optional, when the app is shipped: `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `bundle.sh` (writes `--bundles--/app.bundle`), `license.txt`, `readme.md`.

## Recognizable application folders

**Repository policy:** runtime code and inputs belong in the framework folders above. Classify a file by its consumer, rather than creating a new top-level folder for every concern. `docs/` is for development material; the running application must not read it. Development tools may read evaluation fixtures and reference projects there.

The Forge reorganization is a concrete application of this policy:

| Material | Location | Consumer |
|---|---|---|
| Enabled-language catalogue | `private/languages.json` | Application and validation tools |
| Interface translations | `resources/<lang>.resource` | Native localization |
| SQL, migration notes and maintenance units | `private/database/` | Startup, installation and maintenance |
| Evaluation fixtures and recorded checks | `docs/evaluations/` | Development tools and reviewers |
| Investigation reports and reproductions | `docs/findings/` | Developers |
| Standalone reference applications | `docs/examples/<name>/` | Readers and example checks |

A language catalogue is configuration data, not the interface translation store. Database-backed editorial translations remain in their existing database. Moving a file does not authorize a storage migration.

Use `public/` only when a browser or public client is intended to retrieve the file. Use `private/` for files the application needs internally. Exclude credentials, local databases and development documentation from deployment archives; whitelist the specific private paths required by the runtime rather than packaging the entire directory. Generated assets are not hand-edited source.

The root `database.sql` and dated upgrades used by OpenPlatform and Todomator remain valid existing layouts. When grouping internal SQL files, put the group under `private/database/` rather than creating an application-level `database/` folder. This is repository policy, not a restriction of the Total.js loader. The `database/` folder in this conventions repository is a documentation zone, not an application runtime directory.

Source: Forge's `private/languages.json`, `private/database/`, `modules/i18n.js`, `definitions/benchmarks.js`, `tools/make-package.js`, `tools/with-test-app.js` and `docs/examples/taskboard/`. See [sources and scope](sources.md).

## index.js

The start script is the same in every app and has almost no logic:

```js
require('total5');

var options = {};
options.release = process.argv.indexOf('--release') !== -1;
options.servicemode = process.argv.indexOf('--service') !== -1 || process.argv.indexOf('--servicemode') !== -1;

F.run(options);
```

Run it with `node index.js 8000` (add `--release` for release mode).

## Where things go

- **A route** follows the app's existing pattern: `controllers/*.js` / plugin `index.js`, or the action's `route:` property (Dashboard/IoT/Todomator).
- **Business logic** belongs in actions: usually `schemas/` or `plugins/<name>/schemas/`; compact plugins may declare actions in `index.js` (Dashboard).
- **Shared helpers** hang from `FUNC` (`FUNC.notify`, `FUNC.save`) and live in `definitions/func.js`.
- **Shared state in memory** hangs from `MAIN` (the app) or `REPO` (cached lookups, e.g. `REPO.tags`).
- **Startup work** (config defaults, loading caches, registering UI components) goes in `ON('ready', ...)` in `definitions/init.js`.
- **Authentication** is one `AUTH(...)` in `definitions/auth.js`.

## Files and folders

- All lowercase, words separated by `-`, never `_`: `search-results.html`.
- Static files by type: `/img/`, `/js/`, `/css/`, `/fonts/`, `/videos/`.
- One plugin per feature, named after the feature: `plugins/redirects`, `plugins/users`.
- Generated output (`--bundles--/`, `tmp/`, `databases/`) is not edited by hand.

## Checks

- `node --check path/to/file.js` for every JavaScript file you change.
- Start the app and call the route you touched. If the project has no test script, do not say tests passed.

After moving files, update runtime readers, exporters, migration tools, isolated-test setup, package allowlists, ignore rules and documentation links together. Preserve source content and recorded evidence. Verify that the archive includes the new runtime paths and excludes internal documentation and credentials.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/general/javascript-style.md

# JavaScript style

Source: the [official guidelines](https://github.com/totaljs-es/guidelines) plus what the Total.js 5 apps do. Three rules come first, because they decide most of the code you write:

1. **ES5 over ES6.** This repository chooses the ES5 form for new examples; it is a policy, not a claim that all reference apps use ES5.
2. **Total.js first.** Use the framework's prototypes (backend) and Tangular (frontend) before any other function.
3. **No imports from Node.js.** Use the modules Total.js already exposes.

## 1. ES5 over ES6

Write `var`, `function`, classic loops and string helpers. Use an ES6 feature only when there is no ES5 way to do the same.

| Prefer | Instead of |
|---|---|
| `var item = ...;` | `let` / `const` in a function |
| `function(item) { ... }` | `item => ...` |
| `for (var i = 0; i < arr.length; i++)` | long transformation chains or `for...of` in new examples |
| `'Hello {0}'.format(name)` | template literal `` `Hello ${name}` `` |
| `var a = obj.a;` | destructuring, spread, optional chaining |
| `arr.findItem('id', id)` | `arr.find(x => x.id === id)` |

```js
// good
var item = db.redirects.findItem('id', model.id);
if (!item) {
	$.invalid(404);
	return;
}

// avoid
const item = db.redirects.find(m => m.id === model.id);
```

Notes:

- `async` / `await` stays where the framework's own code uses it (`await DATA.find(...).promise($)`): there the ES5 alternative is a callback chain (`.callback($)`), which is also valid when it reads better.
- The apps also use `let`, arrows, `for...of` and `async` functions. The ES5 preference here is a repository default. Do not rewrite unrelated working code merely to make an existing app look uniformly ES5.
- `const` is for module-level constants only: `const ADMIN = { id: 'admin', sa: true };`.
- **Never `for...in` over an array**: it enumerates property names, including enumerable extensions, rather than just indexed values. Use a classic `for` loop.

## 2. Total.js first

### Backend: prototypes

Total.js extends `String`, `Array`, `Number` and `Date`. Before writing a helper, a loop or a regular expression, check whether a prototype does it. These exist in Total.js 5:

- **String:** `format`, `parseJSON`, `parseInt`, `parseFloat`, `parseBoolean`, `parseDate`, `parseConfig`, `parseCSV`, `parseXML`, `slug`, `capitalize`, `pluralize`, `max`, `toSearch`, `toKeywords`, `removeTags`, `encode`, `decode`, `safehtml`, `md5`, `sha1`, `sha256`, `hash`, `crc32`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `isEmail`, `isPhone`, `isURL`, `isJSON`, `isUID`, `isGUID`, `isNumber`, `isBase64`, `isXSS`, `isSQLInjection`, `indent`, `tslash`.
- **Array:** `findItem`, `findIndex`, `findAll`, `findValue`, `remove`, `quicksort`, `trim`, `first`, `last`, `take`, `skip`, `limit`, `group`, `random`, `wait`, `async`.
- **Number:** `format`, `currency`, `round`, `floor`, `fixed`, `between`, `padLeft`, `padRight`, `filesize`, `pluralize`, `discount`, `parseDate`.
- **Date:** `format`, `add`, `diff`, `extend`, `toUTC`, `setTimeZone`, `parseDate`.

```js
var name = '{0} {1}'.format(first, last);                  // not a template literal
var index = items.findIndex('id', id);                     // not findIndex(m => m.id === id)
var data = text.parseJSON();                               // not try { JSON.parse(text) } catch
var slug = title.slug();                                   // not a hand-made regex
var keywords = body.toKeywords();
if (email.isEmail()) { ... }
```

If you are about to write a utility, search the framework source (`utils.js`) first. The helpers of `U.` (e.g. `U.normalize()`) and the globals (`UID()`, `NOW`, `CONF`, `DATA`) come before your own.

### Frontend: Tangular

In jComponent code and plugin HTML, build text and markup with **Tangular** templates (`{{ value }}`, `{{ foreach m in value }}`, `{{ if }}`) and its helpers, not with string concatenation or DOM-building code.

```html
<script type="text/html">
	{{ foreach m in value }}
	<figure class="exec" data-exec="?/edit" data-id="{{ m.id }}">{{ m.url }}</figure>
	{{ end }}
</script>
```

See [plugins-ui](../frontend/plugins-ui.md).

## 3. No imports from Node.js

Do not `require()` Node.js modules. Total.js exposes them:

| Instead of | Use |
|---|---|
| `require('fs')` | `Total.Fs` |
| `require('path')` | `Total.Path` |
| `require('crypto')` | `Total.Crypto` |
| `require('os')` | `Total.Os` |
| `require('http')` / `require('https')` | `Total.Http` / `Total.Https` (for requests prefer `RESTBuilder`) |
| `require('child_process')` | `Total.Child` |
| `require('zlib')` | `Total.Zlib` |
| `require('url')`, `require('util')`, `require('stream')` | `Total.Url`, `Total.Util`, `Total.Stream` |

Also available: `Total.Cluster`, `Total.Dns`, `Total.Net`, `Total.Tls`, `Total.Worker` and `Total.isBundle`. Check availability in the installed version. `Total.Os` is case-sensitive; `Total.OS` is not the exported property. Third-party packages are the last resort: the framework usually covers the need.

```js
// good
var file = PATH.temp('data.json');

// avoid
const Path = require('path');
```

(The official guide shows `const Path = require('path')`. That was for Total.js 4; in Total.js 5 use `Total.Path`.)

Application files run after Total.js has initialized these globals. Bootstrap files still load `total5`, database adapters may need `require('querybuilderpg')`, and standalone Node.js tools (such as this repo's generator) use Node imports. Do not apply app-global rules to a process that has not loaded the framework.

Access application modules through `MODS.name` or `MODS['hyphenated-name']`, rather than repeatedly requiring their file path. Standalone tools may import a shared helper directly; requiring `total5` alone does not populate the module registry. See [definitions and modules](../backend/definitions-and-modules.md).

## Formatting

- Indent with **tabs** (width 4). No trailing white space.
- End every statement with `;`.
- Short strings in `'` apostrophes.
- A condition with one statement has no braces and no blank line:

```js
if (!item)
	return;

item && refresh();     // fine for a simple expression
```

## Variables and names

- Common names, the same in every project: `id`, `name`, `value`, `email`, `items` / `arr` (a collection), `item`, `tmp`, `dtcreated`, `dtupdated`.

| Thing | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Files, folders | lowercase, `-` | `form-offer.html` |
| Actions | `Collection\|verb` (pipe; exposed to MCP as `Collection_verb`) | `Redirects\|save` |
| Schemas | plural, first letter upper case; `@Name` for a reusable input; `\|` separates nested names, never `/` or `\` | `NEWSCHEMA('Tickets', ...)`, `'@Reports\|Categories'` |
| API routes | lowercase, `_` between collection and verb | `tickets_create` |
| Plugins, components, `FUNC.`, `MAIN.`, `REPO.` keys | lowercase | `FUNC.refreshtags` |
| Table and column names | lowercase | `tbl_user`, `dtcreated` |

## Framework globals

Use the globals that exist instead of writing your own: `UID()` for identifiers, `NOW` for the current date, `CONF` for config, `DATA` for the database, `EMPTYARRAY` / `EMPTYOBJECT` for read-only defaults.

```js
model.id = UID();
model.dtcreated = NOW;
```

## Comments

A comment says why, in one or two lines, above the code it explains. Do not narrate what the next line does.

## Dependencies

Avoid adding any. If the framework has a helper (`RESTBuilder`, `FILESTORAGE`, `U.*`, `DATA`, a prototype), use it.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/backend/actions.md

# Actions

Source: CMS `plugins/redirects/schemas/redirects.js`, OpenPlatform `plugins/setup/schemas/groups.js`, Todomator `schemas/tickets.js` and framework `builders.js`. Examples adapt IDs to this repo's pipe default and retain only the relevant fields.

An action is one unit of server logic: a name, the input it accepts, who may call it, and a function. Define it with `NEWACTION` in a `schemas/` file.

```js
NEWACTION('Redirects|save', {
	name: 'Save redirect',
	input: 'id,*url,*target,permanent:Boolean',
	permissions: 'redirects,admin',
	action: function($, model) {

		if (model.id) {
			var item = MAIN.db.redirects.findItem('id', model.id);
			if (!item) {
				$.invalid(404);
				return;
			}
			item.dtupdated = NOW;
			item.url = model.url;
			item.target = model.target;
			item.permanent = model.permanent;
		} else {
			model.id = UID();
			model.dtcreated = NOW;
			MAIN.db.redirects.push(model);
		}

		FUNC.save();
		$.success();
	}
});
```

## Naming

`Collection|verb`, collection in plural and capitalized: `Tickets|list`, `Groups|create`, `Users|remove`. Separate the two parts with a pipe `|`.

Use `|` between parts of action and schema names, never `/` or `\`: `Tickets|list`, `Reports|Categories|list`, `@Reports|Categories`. A simple name such as `Tickets` or `@Group` needs no separator. This is the Total.js convention adopted by this repository, including grouped and nested names.

Some reference snapshots contain slash names; they are historical observations, not the naming rule to reproduce. When correcting them, update registrations, route targets, `ACTION` / `$.action` calls and direct action-name `tapi()` calls together. Check automatically generated endpoint names and existing external callers; preserve public URLs with explicit routes or compatibility mappings where needed. Do not change URL path separators or plugin method paths such as `?/refresh`: this rule applies to action/schema names.

The framework's MCP sanitizer maps both `/` and `|` to `_`; the pipe convention is our naming choice, not an MCP requirement. See [sources](../general/sources.md).

The usual verbs:

| Verb | Does | Input |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | returns a collection, often with `autoquery` | query string |
| `read` | returns one record | `params: '*id:UID'` |
| `create` | inserts, answers with the new id | `input` |
| `update` | modifies one record | `params` + `input` |
| `save` | create or update by `id` | `input` with optional `id` |
| `remove` | deletes or flags one record | `params` |

Always give the action a human `name:` ("Save redirect"): it is used in logs and tools.

## Input and params

- `input:` is the body, `params:` is the route parameters (`{id}`), `query:` is the query string.
- A text spec: `'*name,color:Color,icon:Icon,permissions:[String]'`. A leading `*` makes a field required. After `:` goes the type (`Boolean`, `Number`, `UID`, `Email`, `Phone`, `Color`, `Date`, `String(100)`, `[String]`).
- Reuse a definition with a named schema and `@`:

```js
NEWSCHEMA('@Group', '*name,color:Color,icon:Icon,reference,permissions:[String]');

NEWACTION('Groups|create', {
	name: 'Create group',
	input: '@Group',
	action: async function($, model) { /* ... */ }
});
```

- Route parameters arrive in `$.params`, not as an argument: `$.params.id`.
- A list typed `*field:[String]` is required: an empty list counts as missing. If empty is valid, drop the `*`.

## Answering

| Call | Use |
|---|---|
| `$.callback(data)` | return data (a record, a list, an id) |
| `$.success()` / `$.success(id)` | the success answer of the app (`DEF.onSuccess`: by default `{ success: true }`, with the value if you pass one) |
| `$.invalid(404)` | not found; the number is the HTTP status |
| `$.invalid('@(Text for the user)')` | validation or business error; `@(...)` marks it for translation |

Complete each response path once. Use an early `return` when code would otherwise fall through after answering; a terminal callback does not need a redundant return. A delegated `.callback($)` or `.callback($.done(id))` also completes the action.

## Permissions

`permissions: 'redirects,admin'` uses the app's `UNAUTHORIZED` policy. Preserve the app's authorization mechanism: some actions use `permissions`, others `user: true`, `sa`, or an explicit `UNAUTHORIZED($, ...)` check. Authentication and access to a particular record are separate checks. Menu visibility grants no server access.

For a protected action that may also be called internally, declare the appropriate action-level check; the `+` on an HTTP route alone does not protect other invocation paths. `public: true` in reference code is not proof that an endpoint is anonymous; inspect the route and action checks. See `builders.js` action execution in the framework source.

## Async and data

Actions are `async` when they await `DATA` calls. Pass `$` to `.promise($)` so errors answer the request for you:

```js
action: async function($) {
	var params = $.params;
	var model = await DATA.read('op.tbl_group').id(params.id).error('@(Group not found)').promise($);
	$.callback(model);
}
```

See [queries](../database/queries.md) for `DATA`.

## Calling one action from another

`$.action('Items|types').promise()` (or `ACTION('Items|types', model).promise()` outside a request). Keep shared pieces in an action instead of copying code.

## Grouped schemas are also Total.js 5

Todomator uses `NEWSCHEMA('Tickets', function(schema) { schema.action('list', { ... }); });`. Do not classify every `NEWSCHEMA` as Total.js 4: reusable input definitions and grouped actions exist in the inspected v5 framework. Keep the target project's established form and verify any API before migrating it.

## Keep an action small

Split a repeated operation or a distinct responsibility when it improves readability. Length alone is not a reason to add a helper or an action chain. Large filter builders (e.g. a `makefilter($, builder)` function inside the schema) stay next to the actions that use them.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/backend/routes-and-auth.md

# Routes and authentication

## Where routes live

In `exports.install` of a file in `controllers/` or of a plugin's `index.js`. One line per route, aligned in columns.

```js
exports.install = function() {

	// Tickets
	ROUTE('+API    ?       -tickets                   --> Tickets|list');
	ROUTE('+API    ?       -tickets_detail/{id}       --> Tickets|read');
	ROUTE('+API    ?       +tickets_create            --> Tickets|create', 1024 * 10);
	ROUTE('+API    ?       +tickets_update/{id}       --> Tickets|update', 1024 * 10);
	ROUTE('+API    ?       -tickets_remove/{id}       --> Tickets|remove');

};
```

Group the lines with a short comment per collection.

## Reading an API route

```
ROUTE('+API    ?    +tickets_create    --> Tickets|create', 1024 * 10);
        |      |     |                     |                |
        |      |     |                     |                max body size in bytes
        |      |     |                     the action
        |      |     "+" the request has a body (input), "-" it has none
        |      the URL of the endpoint; "?" is replaced by CONF.$api ("/api/" by default)
        "+" only for logged-in users; without it the route is public
```

- Endpoint names are lowercase with `_`: `tickets_create`, `users_remove/{id}`. `{id}` fills `$.params.id`.
- Use `-` for reads and removals, `+` for creates and updates.
- A plugin may bind the endpoint to its own base: `ROUTE('+API /setup/ -users --> Users|list')`.
- Without a size, the default body limit applies. Give a limit to routes that take larger bodies.

## Other routes

```js
ROUTE('+GET    /setup/', setup);         // a page, only for logged-in users
ROUTE('POST    /notify/', notify);       // a public route with a handler function
ROUTE('+POST    ?/upload/    @upload <10MB    --> Files|insert');   // an upload: @upload for multipart, <10MB for the size
```

A handler function is `function($)`. Prefer an API route plus an action; use a plain handler for pages, files and webhooks.

## A route declared in the action

`NEWACTION` also accepts `route: '+API ?'` (or `route: true`) and registers the endpoint itself. This is used throughout Dashboard and IoT, and by standalone Todomator actions. It is not restricted to small apps. CMS/OpenPlatform also use explicit controller or plugin routes. Follow one registration style for the feature; do not add a duplicate explicit route for an action that already registers its own.

In the inspected framework `route: true` builds an API route, adding authentication when `user` or `permissions` requires it. An explicit route string controls its own prefix; inspect it rather than assuming all `route:` forms imply authentication. Automatic endpoint names come from action IDs. Preserve their spelling in `tapi()` calls.

## Authentication

One `AUTH` in `definitions/auth.js`. It decides who the request is and calls `$.success(user)` or `$.invalid()`.

```js
AUTH(function($) {
	var token = $.headers['x-token'];
	if (token) {
		if (BLOCKED($, 10)) {      // too many wrong tries from this client
			$.invalid();
			return;
		}
		if (token === CONF.token) {
			BLOCKED($, -1);        // forget the failures
			$.success(BOT);
		} else
			$.invalid();
	} else
		$.invalid();
});
```

- The user object is small: `{ id, name, sa, permissions }`. `sa` marks a super administrator.
- Use `BLOCKED($, limit)` to rate-limit failed logins: it counts tries per `$.ip` and returns `true` once the limit is passed (`BLOCKED($, -1)` clears the count). Because it keys on `$.ip`, it inherits the `X-Forwarded-For` caveat below.
- `+` routes require authentication; action-level checks apply when configured. Test authenticated, anonymous and insufficient-permission requests.
- `$.ip` takes the first value of `X-Forwarded-For`, which a client can forge. For security limits use `$.req.socket.remoteAddress`, or trust the header only behind your own proxy.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/backend/definitions-and-modules.md

# Definitions and modules

## definitions/

Files here are loaded when the app starts. They export nothing: they register things on the framework. One file per concern.

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `auth.js` | the single `AUTH(...)` |
| `init.js` | config defaults and `ON('ready', ...)`: load caches, register UI components |
| `func.js` | shared helpers as `FUNC.name = function() {}` |
| `db.js` | shared state objects (`MAIN.id`, `MAIN.db`) |

```js
// definitions/init.js
CONF.version = '1';
if (!CONF.cdn)
	CONF.cdn = 'https://cdn.componentator.com';

ON('ready', function() {
	setTimeout(FUNC.load, 500);
	COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,input,form,validate,...', true);
});
```

```js
// definitions/func.js
FUNC.refreshtags = async function() {
	REPO.tags = await DATA.find('tbl_tag').fields('id,search').promise();
};
```

- Helpers are named in lowercase without separators: `FUNC.refreshtags`, `FUNC.notify`.
- Use `ON('ready')` for anything that needs the app and the database to be up.
- `EMIT('configure')` / `ON('configure')` is how parts of the app react to a config change.

## config

A plain file, one `key : value` per line. Read it with `CONF.key`. Settings the framework owns start with `$`: `$api`, `$minifyjs`. Secrets (keys, database URLs) do not belong in a repository: keep them in the deployment config.

## modules/

A module is an integration with another system or a self-contained service (`cdn.js`, `openplatform.js`, `visitors.js`). Total.js loads `modules/*.js` automatically and registers the exports under `MODS`, using `exports.id` or the filename without its extension. The loader calls `exports.install()` when that method exists; a module exposing reusable methods does not need an empty installer.

Use that registry from initialized application code. Adapted from CMS `plugins/dashboard/schemas/dashboard.js`:

```js
var data = MODS.visitors.today();
var visitors = MODS.visitors.instance.visitors;
```

Hyphenated IDs use bracket access, for example `MODS['knowledge-source']`. Do not repeatedly import an application module with `require(PATH.root('modules/...'))`. Name application modules `.js`; in the inspected loader, a `.cjs` helper is not automatically registered by the `modules` scan.

`MODS` exists after framework initialization, but an entry exists only after its module loads. Read another module from an exported method or an appropriate lifecycle callback; do not depend on sibling filename order or introduce circular initialization. Work needing application state or a database belongs in the existing ready/configure lifecycle. An automatically called `install()` must not require arguments supplied only by a later controller.

A standalone Node tool does not acquire loaded application modules merely by requiring `total5`. It may import a shared CommonJS helper directly. Preserve that execution boundary when code is shared with validators or maintenance tools; do not replace valid CLI imports with an unpopulated `MODS` entry. The `total5` bootstrap and third-party database adapters also retain their required imports.

Keep a module independent: it reads `CONF`, not another integration's private internals. Some existing integrations expose a dedicated global such as `OpenPlatform`; preserve that public contract when present. New application module consumers use `MODS`.

Sources: framework5 `index.js` (module loading and optional installer), `global.js` (`MODS = F.modules`), CMS dashboard actions, and Forge controllers/definitions after its module reorganization.

## Shared state

- `MAIN`: the application's own state (`MAIN.db`, `MAIN.cache`).
- `REPO`: cached lookups that the UI also needs (`REPO.tags`, `REPO.ui`).
- `FUNC`: functions shared by actions and controllers.
- `MODS`: automatically registered application module exports.

Do not create new globals. Hang things from these three.

## Config in the database

When settings live in a table (`cl_config`), load them with `LOADCONFIG(rows)` and emit `configure`, as `FUNC.reconfigure` does in Todomator.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/backend/storage-and-integrations.md

# Storage and integrations

Choose the model already used by the feature. The apps do not all store data in SQL.

## Persistence and cache ownership

| Model | Source | How to extend it |
|---|---|---|
| CMS metadata in memory, serialized to FileStorage | CMS `definitions/db.js`, `definitions/func.js`, redirects actions | Mutate the existing collection, call `FUNC.save()`, refresh affected rendering caches when necessary |
| SQL through `DATA` and `querybuilderpg` | OpenPlatform groups; Todomator `definitions/init.js`, `schemas/tickets.js` | Keep projections, filters, identifiers, response shapes and adapter initialization |
| Named persisted memory object | Dashboard `modules/openplatform.js`, `plugins/views/index.js` | Keep `MEMORIZE` object ownership and existing save hooks |
| Flow state | FlowOS `definitions/init.js` | Keep flow load/save lifecycle and websocket permissions together |

The last two are observations, with no Enterprise code reproduced here. Do not switch models during a conventions cleanup.

CMS `FUNC.load` reads `meta`, initializes defaults, compiles widgets and emits reload. `FUNC.save` excludes compiled references before serialization. Changing a page/widget can therefore require cache refresh as well as saving metadata. Follow the feature's actual invalidation path rather than inventing a second cache.

## Outgoing requests

Use `RESTBuilder` and the existing integration configuration. The MIT Todomator source ends `schemas/tickets.js` with a small `TicketCallback` integration using `RESTBuilder.POST(...).callback(NOOP)`. Its notification is intentionally independent; use explicit error handling when an action's result depends on the remote call.

Illustrative request-dependent pattern (adapted to the request style in the framework's `builders.js`, `RESTP.promise`):

```js
var response = await RESTBuilder.GET(CONF.serviceurl).promise($);
```

Check the remote status and response shape required by the integration before returning success. Do not assume a network-success callback proves a valid business response. In a job without `$`, use an error-first callback or handle `.promise()` rejection. Reuse project timeouts, authentication and cancellation conventions when present; verify support in the installed version.

## Configuration and lifecycle

Read configuration through `CONF` and follow the target app's settings loader. CMS and Todomator use `LOADCONFIG` and `configure` hooks; their service listeners refresh or reload state periodically. Do not add a parallel environment/config system to a feature that already has settings.

- Startup work belongs in the existing ready/init path.
- React to configuration changes through the existing `ON('configure', ...)` / `EMIT('configure')` flow.
- Repeated maintenance uses the app's `ON('service', function(counter) { ... })` convention where available, rather than one timer per action call.
- Keep request-dependent errors observable. Use `ERROR('context')` where the surrounding app expects a logging callback; use `NOOP` only for deliberately ignored results.

Sources: CMS `definitions/init.js`, `definitions/func.js`; Todomator `definitions/init.js`, `definitions/func.js`, `definitions/auth.js`. Do not copy development credentials or permissive demo auth from a reference app into a new deployment.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/backend/gotchas.md

# Gotchas of the server

Things that behave differently from what you would guess. Each one is a rule.

## Answers

- In an **action**, `$.callback(data)` returns data. In a plain **route handler** (`function($)`), `$.callback(err, value)` takes the error first: answer with `$.json(data)` instead.
- `$.invalid(404)`: a number above 399 sets the HTTP status (an omitted error becomes 401 in the inspected `ErrorBuilder.push`; use an explicit code for clarity). `$.invalid('@(text)')` answers with the message; its second argument is the `path` of the field the error belongs to, not a status code.
- On a handler you can also set the status yourself: `$.response.status = 401; $.json(...)`.

## Request data

- Route parameters (`{id}`) are in `$.params`.
- In a controller, `$.body` is parsed and `$.payload` holds the buffered raw body for the supported body-parsing path. In an action, `$.payload` / `model` is the action input, not that raw HTTP buffer. For webhook signatures use the controller context and verify the route flags/content type preserve the bytes you sign.
- `$.ip` is the first `X-Forwarded-For` value: forgeable. Use `$.req.socket.remoteAddress` for security limits.
- When changing CSRF handling, check the installed framework's `Controller.prototype.csrf` and view directive support; verify token generation and validation together. Do not introduce an alternative transport solely because a past app needed one.
- Session checks depend on the app's authentication module. Inspect its cookie, token and user-agent checks before assuming a session is portable between clients.

## Schemas and input

- A `Boolean` that is absent is `false`. Use `partial: true` when absence must mean "unchanged".
- With `partial`, a `null` number is ignored; use `0` for "none".
- `*field:[String]` rejects an empty list; drop the `*` if empty is allowed.
- Never `for...in` over an array. Use a classic `for` loop.

## Served JavaScript and static files

- `node --check` does not validate the release minifier or browser execution. Check the served asset in the installed version when changing regular expressions or template syntax. Diagnose a reproducible failure before disabling `$minifyjs`; do not make a global configuration change as a style fix.
- In release, static files are served from memory: restart the app after changing them. Browsers also cache: force a reload while testing.

## Data

- NoSQL: `NOSQL('x').find().where(...)`; `.sort(field, true)` is **descending**. Updates append a line and mark the old one, so the file grows until it is cleaned.
- NoSQL dates arrive on the server as `Date`, on the client as text.

## Tests

- `opt.config` passed to `Total.run` is overridden by `(env)` entries of the config: set `process.env` first.
- Before running a translation extractor, check its scan scope in the installed version and keep generated/vendor directories out of the input. Verify the resulting `.resource` files.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/database/sql-scripts.md

# SQL scripts (PostgreSQL)

Source: the [official guidelines](https://github.com/totaljs-es/guidelines) and the `database.sql` files of Todomator and OpenPlatform.

## Files

- `database.sql` holds the whole current schema, so a new installation needs one file.
- Preserve the existing root SQL-file layout in apps that use it. When grouping SQL and maintenance files in a directory, use `private/database/`; update application readers, migration tools and package allowlists together. This layout policy does not change the SQL contract. See [project structure](../general/project-structure.md).
- A change to an existing installation goes in a separate script next to it, named with a date: `database-2024-10-30.sql`. OpenPlatform does this; Todomator also has `database_1-5.sql` by version. Prefer the dated name with dashes, as the file rule requires.
- The first lines of an upgrade script say which version it upgrades from and that it must run before the app starts.
- Inside a script, order the objects: **tables, views, functions and stored procedures, indexes**, each part under a banner comment (`-- TABLES`, `-- VIEWS`, `-- INDEXES`).
- Todomator wraps its script in `BEGIN; ... COMMIT;` so that it applies completely or not at all.

## Names

All lowercase, singular.

| Object | Prefix | Example |
|---|---|---|
| table | `tbl_` | `tbl_user`, `tbl_ticket_time` |
| code list (rarely changes, used for choices) | `cl_` | `cl_status`, `cl_type` |
| view | `view_` | `view_ticket` |
| stored procedure | `sp_` | `sp_user` |
| function | `fn_` | `fn_user` |

Name indexes `<table>_idx<what>`: `tbl_ticket_idxstatus`. Name foreign keys `<table>_<column>_fkey`.

## Columns

- Type `text`, not `varchar`. Lists are `_text`, structured data `json` or `jsonb`, small numbers `int2`, dates `timestamp`, flags `bool`.
- `id` is the primary key, `text`, filled in the code with `UID()`. A foreign key is the table plus `id`: `userid`, `folderid`, `parentid`.
- Dates start with `dt`: `dtcreated`, `dtupdated`, `dtremoved`. Booleans start with `is`: `isremoved`, `ispublic`, `isdisabled`.
- Use the same names for the same thing in every table: `name`, `body`, `search`, `sortindex`, `icon`, `color`.
- When it fits, every table has `id`, `name` and `dtcreated`.
- `dtcreated` defaults to UTC now: `DEFAULT timezone('utc'::text, now())`.
- A column that lists search keywords is called `search`.

## Order of the columns

Identifiers first, then main fields, numbers, booleans, and dates last. Then the constraints and the primary key.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "public"."tbl_ticket" (
	"id" text NOT NULL,
	"folderid" text,
	"ownerid" text,
	"name" text,
	"search" text,
	"attrs" json,
	"worked" int4 DEFAULT 0,
	"ispublic" bool DEFAULT false,
	"isremoved" bool DEFAULT false,
	"dtupdated" timestamp,
	"dtcreated" timestamp DEFAULT timezone('utc'::text, now()),
	CONSTRAINT "tbl_ticket_folderid_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("folderid") REFERENCES "public"."tbl_folder"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
	PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);
```

## Code lists

A `cl_` table holds the choices of the app and is read once into memory.

```sql
CREATE TABLE "public"."cl_status" (
	"id" text NOT NULL,
	"name" text,
	"icon" text,
	"color" text,
	"sortindex" int2 DEFAULT 0,
	PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);
```

## Format

Tabs (width 4), no useless casts (`name <> 'x'`, not `name <> 'x'::text`), one statement per `;`, a trailing `;` on every command.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/database/queries.md

# Queries with `DATA`

For SQL-backed features, Total.js uses `DATA` and the configured database adapter (for example `querybuilderpg`). Do not introduce SQL into a FileStorage/MEMORIZE feature just to match this page. Use the builder for what it can express; write raw SQL only when needed.

For request-bound results use `.promise($)` (in an async action), `.callback($)` or `.callback($.done(id))`. In jobs and shared helpers without a request use `.promise()` with explicit error handling or an error-first callback. Do not invent a request context. Some source apps enqueue background writes without awaiting them; do not copy that when the response depends on the write succeeding.

## Read

```js
// one record
var item = await DATA.read('tbl_user').fields('id,name').id(params.id).error('@(User not found)').promise($);

// several
var items = await DATA.find('tbl_tag').fields('id,search').where('folderid', id).promise($);

// values from a list
var apps = await DATA.find('op.tbl_app_permission').fields('id,appid').in('id', permissions).promise($);
```

- `.fields('a,b')` selects columns; name them, do not read `*`.
- `.id(value)` filters by the primary key.
- `.error('@(text)')` or `.error(404)` answers with that error when nothing is found. It is what turns a missing row into a 404.

## A list for the UI

`autoquery` reads the query string (`?q=`, `sort`, `page`, `limit`) and builds the query. Name the allowed fields and their types, a default sort and a maximum page size:

```js
NEWACTION('Groups|list', {
	name: 'List of groups',
	action: function($) {
		DATA.find('op.view_group').autoquery($.query, 'id:UID,name,color,icon,users:Number,dtcreated:Date,dtupdated:Date', 'dtcreated_desc', 100).callback($);
	}
});
```

A reusable joined list often reads from a `view_`. IoT also uses `DATA.list(...)` for paginated output; OpenPlatform uses `DATA.find(...)`. Preserve the response shape expected by the UI rather than swapping these because their query chains look similar.

## Write

```js
model.id = UID();
model.dtcreated = NOW;
await DATA.insert('tbl_ticket_time', model).promise($);

model.dtupdated = NOW;
await DATA.modify('op.tbl_group', model).id(params.id).error('@(Group not found)').promise($);

await DATA.remove('tbl_tag').id(params.id).error(404).promise($);
await DATA.remove('tbl_notification').where('ticketid', params.id).where('typeid', 'logwork').promise($);
```

- Fill `id` with `UID()` and the dates with `NOW` in the action, not in the database.
- Remove fields that are not columns before `insert` / `modify` (`model.permissions = undefined`).
- Update or insert in one call: `DATA.modify('tbl_x', data, true).id(id).insert(fn, params)`.

## Success after a write

When a write should return the app's success envelope rather than its raw database result, the reference apps use:

```js
DATA.remove('tbl_tag').id($.params.id).error(404).callback($.done($.params.id));
```

Adapted from Todomator's `schemas/tickets.js` (`reset`). Keep the established response contract. A raw `.callback($)` and `$.done(id)` are not interchangeable responses.

## Conditions

`where(field, value)`, `in(field, array)`, `notin(field, array)`, `search(field, keyword)`, `or(function(b) { b.search('name', m); b.search('email', m); })`.

```js
var keywords = text.toKeywords(true, true);
for (var i = 0; i < keywords.length; i++)
	builder.search('a.search', keywords[i]);
```

## Raw SQL

`DATA.query('UPDATE tbl_ticket a SET worked=(SELECT ...) WHERE a.id=$1', [id]).promise($)`.

- Prefer parameters (`$1`) over building the text.
- When a value must go into the text, escape it with `PG_ESCAPE(value)` before `.format()`. Never concatenate user input.

## Schemas (namespaces)

A table can be addressed with its schema: `op.tbl_user`. Keep the prefix consistent inside one file.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/frontend/components.md

# Components (jComponent)

For widgets, forms, lists, inputs and every other piece of UI, **use a component that already exists**. If none fits, **create a component** (do not build the piece with ad hoc markup and scripts). Load catalogue components with `COMPONENTATOR()`; custom app-owned components remain normal app assets.

## 1. Look for the component first

The catalogue of jComponent components, with the options and examples of each, is in Forge: <https://forge.totaljs.es/es/components/> (also in `/en/components/`).

Before writing UI:

1. Find the component that does the job (input, form, listing, datagrid, notify, menu, approve...).
2. Read its page: what it does, its **configuration** and its context (what path and data it expects, what it needs around it).
3. Use it from markup with `<ui-component name="..." path="..." config="...">`.

Machine-readable forms of the same catalogue (use these from code or an agent):

| What | URL |
|---|---|
| One component as markdown | `https://forge.totaljs.es/en/components/<name>.md` (e.g. `input.md`) |
| The whole catalogue as one text | `https://forge.totaljs.es/llms-components.txt` |
| The catalogue as JSON lines | `https://forge.totaljs.es/components/dataset.jsonl` |
| Index of all Forge pages | `https://forge.totaljs.es/index.json` |

Each page carries its framework version (`jcomponent@20`) and a content hash, so you can tell which version a rule refers to.

## Match the UI version first

The inspected CMS admin loads `spa.min@19`, while Dashboard, IoT and FlowOS use `@20`; Todomator also mixes shells. A catalogue entry for jComponent 20 does not prove its markup or options work in 19. Check the actual layout, bundle and nearby screen before using a component or copying `PLUGIN`/binding syntax. A backend Total.js 5 dependency does not select the browser UI major version.

## Preferred components

When several components could do the job, use these:

| For | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Form fields (text, email, phone, password, multiline, checkbox, select, date...) | `input` (j-Input) | One component for every field: `type` chooses the kind. It replaces j-Textbox and j-Dropdown. |
| A box with a fixed height and scroll | `viewbox` | `height` is a percentage, `parent` is the container (or `window`), `scroll` / `scrollbar` control scrolling. |
| Loaders | `loading` | Reacts to the `@showloading` and `@hideloading` flags; `style` picks the look (1 = spinner, 2 = line at the top). |
| Tables and data grids | `datagrid` | For single page and enterprise apps: filters, sorting, pages, `height` modes (`auto`, `fluid`, `parent`). |
| Buttons and calls to functions | `exec` | See below. |
| Predefined design (panels, toolbars, badges, messages, listings, tabs, dark mode) | `intranetcss` | Ready-made CSS classes; see below. |

### exec: buttons and function calls

`exec` is a singleton that works for the whole page: any element with the class `exec` calls a function when it is clicked. Do not add `onclick` handlers or `addEventListener` for buttons.

```html
<button class="exec" data-exec="?/create"><i class="ti ti-plus-circle"></i>@(Create)</button>
<span class="exec" data-exec="?/options" data-prevent="true">...</span>
<a class="exec" data-href="/offers/">@(Offers)</a>
```

- `data-exec="NAME"`: the function to call, with the form `function(element, event)`. A `?` calls a method of the current plugin (`?/create` is `exports.create`).
- `data-prevent="true"`: stops the click from going further (for a button inside a clickable row).
- `data-href="URL"`: redirects instead of calling a function.
- Double click and context menu use the same attributes with a suffix: `data-exec2` (class `exec2`) and `data-exec3` (class `exec3`).

### intranetcss: predefined design

`intranetcss` is a component made only of CSS. It brings the shared look of the intranet apps, with a dark mode, so a screen does not need its own style for the common pieces:

- containers: `.panel` (with `label` and `.toolbar`), `.padding`, `.divider`, `.bg-smoke`
- lists and menus: `.listing`, `.listing2`, `.nav`, `.tabmenu`, `.tabmenu2`, `.iconmenu`, `.keyvalue`
- messages and badges: `.message`, `.message-success`, `.message-error`, `.message-alert`, `.badge` (with colors and sizes)
- sizes: `.small`, `.medium`, `.large`

Use these classes before writing new CSS (see [css](css.md)). The component is not in the Forge catalogue; its source (version 5) is served by the component download service.

## 2. If it does not exist, create a component

A piece of UI that has behaviour is a component, not a block of script inside a page.

```js
COMPONENT('name', function(self, config, cls) {
	// keep the names: "self", "config" and "cls"
});
```

- Names of components, plugins, variables and settings in **lowercase**.
- Keep at most 2-3 levels of nesting in objects.
- Avoid `_` in variable names.
- **Think reusable**: a component takes its data from `path` and its options from `config`, and knows nothing about the screen that uses it.
- Use the same name across projects for the same thing. Check the catalogue before choosing one.

## 3. Load components with COMPONENTATOR()

For shared catalogue components, use the app's `COMPONENTATOR()` bundle. App-owned components load through the app's existing assets. For example, in `definitions/init.js`:

```js
ON('ready', function() {
	COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,page,viewbox,input,form,validate,loading,datagrid,intranetcss,message,menu,approve,notify,errorhandler', true);
});
```

`COMPONENTATOR(name, components, removeprev, attrs)`:

- `name`: the name of the bundle (`'ui'`).
- `components`: the components of the bundle, comma-separated, without the `j-` prefix.
- `removeprev` (default `true`): deletes the older bundles of the same name when the list changes.
- `attrs`: optional extra parameters for the bundle.

The framework downloads the bundle once, saves it in `public/` as `ui-<name>-<hash>.min.js` and stores its address in `REPO.<name>`. The layout loads it:

```html
<script src="@{REPO.ui}"></script>
```

Rules:

- One `COMPONENTATOR()` call per bundle (`ui` for the app, `webui` for public pages).
- List **only** the components the app uses: the bundle is what every user downloads.
- When you start using a component, add it to the list; when no screen uses it any more, remove it.
- A component you created yourself is a normal file of the app (`public/` or the plugin's `public/`), not a `COMPONENTATOR()` entry.

## Adapt the official component's appearance

Reuse the official component and its configuration first. A different visual design usually needs a scoped CSS skin, not a copied component implementation or a file that embeds jComponent itself.

Forge at commit `827311e` uses the official `backtotop` through `COMPONENTATOR('webui', 'backtotop', true)` and declares:

```html
<ui-component name="backtotop" class="forge-backtotop" config="icon:ti ti-arrow-up;$init:FUNC.backtotop" data-label="@(Back to top)"></ui-component>
```

Its `public/css/components.css` changes the appearance. Its `public/js/func.js` adds button semantics, a translated accessible name and keyboard focus handling through the native `$init` hook. The official component retains its scrolling and visibility behavior. The hook is needed because the inspected official component renders a span; CSS cannot provide button semantics.

Verify hook timing against the installed runtime and component: the inspected `jComponent/library.js` calls `make` before applying `$init`, so the hook can adapt the generated markup. Keep such hooks small and idempotent, and check Enter, Space, pointer interaction, focus and reduced motion. If a component supplies the required semantics already, use them directly.

Sources: Forge `definitions/ui.js`, `views/layout.html`, `public/js/func.js` and `public/css/components.css` at `827311e`; upstream `j-BackToTop/component.js` in Forge's pinned `vendor/components-master/`; [jComponent source](https://github.com/totaljs/jComponent), `library.js`, component creation and reconfiguration. This is a maintained-app example, not a claim that every Total.js app needs an initialization hook.

## 4. Quick check

- Is there a component for this in the catalogue? Use it.
- Did you read its configuration and context before using it? Do.
- Is it in the `COMPONENTATOR()` list? Add it.
- Is there none? Create a reusable `COMPONENT('name', ...)` and use it from markup.

See [plugins-ui](plugins-ui.md) for how screens and forms use components, and [views-and-layout](views-and-layout.md) for the layout that loads the bundle.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/frontend/plugins-ui.md

# Plugins with UI

A feature of an app is a **plugin**: a folder with a server part and a UI part that the framework loads and the app shell mounts. The CMS admin (pages, layouts, redirects, settings...) and the Todomator users screen are made this way.

```
plugins/redirects/
	index.js              server: metadata + routes
	schemas/redirects.js  actions (see backend/actions.md)
	public/index.html     the screen: markup + <script>PLUGIN(...)</script>
	public/form.html      the form that opens over the screen
```

## Server part: index.js

```js
exports.icon = 'ti ti-exchange';
exports.name = '@(Redirects)';
exports.position = 3;
exports.permissions = [{ id: 'redirects', name: 'Redirects' }];
exports.visible = function(user) {
	return user.sa || user.permissions.indexOf('redirects') !== -1 || user.permissions.indexOf('admin') !== -1;
};

exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('+API    ?    -redirects_list               --> Redirects|list');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    +redirects_save               --> Redirects|save');
};
```

- `icon` is a Total Icons class (`ti ti-name`), `name` is translatable with `@(...)`, `position` orders the menu.
- `permissions` declares what the plugin adds; `visible` decides who sees it.
- Routes use the same syntax as everywhere (see [routes-and-auth](../backend/routes-and-auth.md)).

## UI part: a screen

A screen is HTML with a `<ui-plugin>` root and one `PLUGIN(function(exports) { ... })` block. Keep markup, scoped style and logic in the same file. Screens may also include a `virtualwire` toolbar, importer declarations and other app-shell wrappers; copy the nearest screen rather than enforcing exactly one root element.

```html
<style>
	.CLASS .listing2 figure { margin-bottom: 10px; }
</style>

<ui-plugin class="CLASS bg-white">
	<ui-component name="empty" path="?.items" config="parent:auto" class="invisible">
		...
	</ui-component>
</ui-plugin>

<script>
	PLUGIN(function(exports) {

		exports.reload = function() {
			exports.refresh();
		};

		exports.refresh = function() {
			exports.tapi('redirects_list', function(response) {
				exports.set('items', response);
			});
		};

	});
</script>
```

Rules:

- `CLASS` in selectors and class lists is replaced with a unique class for the plugin: it scopes the CSS so plugins do not collide.
- `?` in a path (`?.items`, `?/create`) means "this plugin": `?.items` is the data, `?/create` is `exports.create`.
- `exports.reload` runs every time the screen opens.
- Call the server with `exports.tapi('endpoint_name', data, callback)`. Add `ERROR` after the name (`'redirects_read ERROR'`) to show an error message to the user automatically.
- Set data with `exports.set('items', value)`, or globally with `SET('path @reset', value)`; read the model with `exports.model`.
- Handlers are attached in markup: `class="exec" data-exec="?/edit" data-id="{{ m.id }}"`. Read the attribute with `ATTRD(el)`.
- Text for people is always `@(Text)` so it can be translated.
- Naming: plugin, component and global names in **lowercase**; keep the names `exports`, `self`, `config`, `cls` as they are.

Official guide on names:

```js
// BAD
PLUGIN('Name', function(plugin) { plugin.doSomething = function() {}; });

// GOOD
PLUGIN('name', function(exports) { exports.dosomething = function() {}; });
```

See [binding and forms](binding-and-forms.md) for the importer, model path, submit callback and caller refresh as one connected flow.

## A form

A form is a second file loaded with an `importer` and shown by `miniform` / `form`. It has `?.field` inputs, a `validate` that enables the submit button, and a `submit` function.

```html
<ui-component name="miniform" path="common.form" config="if:CLASS;icon:ti ti-exchange;autofocus:true;reload:?/reload;submit:?/submit;width:400" class="hidden" plugin="CLASS">
	<div class="padding">
		<div class="m">
			<ui-component name="input" path="?.url" config="required:1;placeholder:@(Relative URL address)">@(URL)</ui-component>
		</div>
	</div>
	<nav>
		<ui-component name="validate" path="?">
			<button name="submit" disabled><i class="ti ti-check-circle"></i>@(SUBMIT)</button>
			<button name="cancel">@(Cancel)</button>
		</ui-component>
	</nav>
</ui-component>
```

Open it from the screen:

```js
exports.create = function() {
	SET('formredirect @default', {});
	SET('*form', 'formredirect');
};
```

## Confirm and menu

```js
SETTER('approve/show', '@(Are you sure you want to remove it?)', ':ti ti-trash: @(Remove)', function() {
	exports.tapi('redirects_remove/ ERROR', { id: id }, function() { exports.refresh(); });
});
SETTER('menu/show', opt);
```

## Think reusable

Components, plugins and global names are shared across projects. Before inventing one, look in the [catalogue of components](components.md) and in another app for the same name.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/frontend/views-and-layout.md

# Views and layout

## Layout

The shell of an app is one HTML file in `views/` (`admin.html`, `index.html`). It sets the title, loads the UI library, registers global components once and mounts the plugins.

```html
@{layout('')}
@{title(config.name)}

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
	<meta charset="utf-8" />
	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
	<link href="https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.css" rel="stylesheet" />
	<script src="https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.js"></script>
	<script src="@{REPO.ui}"></script>
	@{import('meta', 'head', 'default.js + func.js', 'default.css', 'favicon.ico')}
</head>
<body class="invisible">

	<ui-component name="exec"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="errorhandler"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="locale" config="requests:1;language:@{language}"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="LAZY menu" config="style:2"></ui-component>

</body>
</html>
```

- Directives start with `@{...}`: `@{title()}`, `@{import()}`, `@{if}` / `@{fi}`, `@{REPO.ui}`, `https://cdn.componentator.com` (a config value).
- Global components are declared once in the layout. `LAZY` loads a component only when it is first used.
- The component bundle is loaded with `COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,input,...', true)` in `definitions/init.js`. List only the components the app uses; see [components](components.md).
- `<body class="invisible">` hides the page until the UI is ready.

## Runtime, bundles and application assets

The example above is adapted from the CMS shell, using this repository's jComponent 20 CDN default for new layouts. The inspected CMS itself uses 19; an existing app requires a deliberate version migration. Forge's public and admin layouts at commit `827311e` demonstrate the 20 setup.

- Load `https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.css` and `https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.js` once per document. The runtime must precede component bundles and scripts that use its APIs.
- `COMPONENTATOR()` downloads the selected components; it does not replace the core runtime. Load the matching `@{REPO.ui}` or `@{REPO.webui}` after the runtime.
- Keep application helpers in app assets, such as `public/js/func.js`, and preserve the existing browser `FUNC` object when extending it. Load helpers before components that call them during initialization.
- Keep the app stylesheet and scoped component skins after the base stylesheet; see [CSS](css.md). Remove embedded copies of the runtime and obsolete custom loaders when adopting this setup.
- An isolated recipe iframe can intentionally use a pinned runtime with its own hashes and evidence. It is a separate document; preserve that version boundary.

Changing asset loading must preserve the existing title, language, canonical and alternate URLs, metadata, structured data, agent discovery links, landmarks and accessible navigation. Check the rendered HTML and browser console, keyboard interaction, mobile layout and reduced-motion behavior. A component initializing successfully does not establish that the whole layout is accessible.

## Translations

Every text a person reads is wrapped in `@(...)`, in views, in plugin HTML and in server messages: `@(Save)`. The text in English is the key.

## Two kinds of pages

- **App screens** (admin, tools): plugin HTML mounted in the layout, driven by `PLUGIN`.
- **Public pages**: server-rendered views returned by a controller (`$.view('index')`) or compiled from the CMS. They carry no `PLUGIN` logic.

## Naming

Lowercase file names with `-`: `search-results.html`, `form-offer.html`.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/frontend/binding-and-forms.md

# Binding and forms as one flow

Source: CMS `plugins/redirects/public/index.html` and `public/form.html`. The following connected example is adapted to the repo's ES5 preference and includes only the fields needed to show the lifecycle. It assumes the CMS shell, jComponent version, importer and `*form` alias setup; it is not a standalone page.

## Screen → model → importer

The screen declares the form importer and opens a model with the same name. The app's importer replaces `CLASS` when loading the form.

```html
<ui-component name="importer" path="common.form" config="if:formredirect;url:/~ID~/form.html"></ui-component>
```

```js
exports.create = function() {
	SET('formredirect @default', {});
	SET('*form', 'formredirect');
};

exports.edit = function(el) {
	var id = ATTRD(el);
	exports.tapi('redirects_read ERROR', { id: id }, function(response) {
		SET('formredirect @reset', response);
		SET('*form', 'formredirect');
	});
};
```

`formredirect`, the form's `CLASS`, the importer condition, `common.form` and `*form` must agree with the target shell. Do not copy the open function into another app without its alias/importer setup. Read data before showing an edit form; initialize a new model before showing create so the previous record does not leak into it.

## Form → submit → caller refresh

```html
<ui-component name="miniform" path="common.form" config="if:CLASS;title:@(Redirect);reload:?/reload;submit:?/submit;width:400" class="hidden" plugin="CLASS">
	<div class="padding">
		<ui-component name="input" path="?.url" config="required:1">@(URL)</ui-component>
		<ui-component name="input" path="?.target" config="required:1">@(Target URL)</ui-component>
	</div>
	<nav>
		<ui-component name="validate" path="?">
			<button name="submit" disabled>@(SUBMIT)</button>
			<button name="cancel">@(Cancel)</button>
		</ui-component>
	</nav>
</ui-component>

<script>
	PLUGIN(function(exports) {

		var caller;

		exports.reload = function() {
			caller = exports.caller;
		};

		exports.submit = function(hide) {
			var model = exports.form;
			exports.tapi('redirects_save ERROR', model, function() {
				hide();
				caller.exec('refresh');
			});
		};

	});
</script>
```

The form component owns the submit/cancel buttons. Ordinary screen buttons use `exec`; do not add a second submit listener. Hide only after a successful response, then refresh the caller. Verify `exports.form` / `exports.model` against the actual UI version and nearby form; they are not names to exchange mechanically.

## Binding and templates

CMS screens bind `?.items` through `ui-bind` and render a `script type="text/html"` with Tangular. Update the model (`exports.set('items', response)`) so the binding owns rendering, rather than keeping a parallel list in the DOM. Use `CLASS` for screen CSS, `?` for local paths and `data-exec="?/method"` for handlers. Preserve the shell's global model paths.

Treat user text as text in templates; do not add raw HTML rendering or string-built event attributes. Backend view directives (`@{...}`), translation markers (`@(...)`) and client Tangular (`{{ ... }}`) are distinct stages. Use the syntax supported by that app's library and compiler; check a working template for block terminators and escaping.

## Translations and icons

English text is the source key: `@(Save)`, `@(Target URL)`, translated through the app's `.resource` files. Keep resource keys, locale component configuration and any new error text synchronized. Avoid hard-coded translated copies in JS conditionals. Use the existing Total Icons `ti ti-*` assets and names from the app, with a label or accessible name for icon-only controls.

## Reusable components

Look for an existing component first. If new behaviour is reusable, use `COMPONENT('name', function(self, config, cls) { ... })` and the lifecycle supported by the installed jComponent version: build the DOM once, update from its bound value, react to configuration changes and release subscriptions/timers when destroyed. Read an existing component of that version for the exact methods. Keep feature permissions, API URLs and page model names in the plugin rather than baking them into the component.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/conventions/main/frontend/css.md

# CSS

Source: the [official guidelines](https://github.com/totaljs-es/guidelines).

- File names lowercase, words separated by `-`.
- **One rule per line**: keep all declarations of a selector on the same line.
- Strings in `'` apostrophes.
- No vendor prefixes. Put `/*auto*/` at the top of the file and Total.js adds them.
- No LESS and no SASS: Total.js CSS supports variables and nested selectors.

```css
/*auto*/

.class { key1: value; key2: value; key3: value; }
.class > div { key1: value; key2: value; }
```

## In plugins

Style that belongs to a screen goes at the top of its HTML file, scoped with `CLASS`:

```html
<style>
	.CLASS .listing2 figure { margin-bottom: 10px; }
	.CLASS .listing2 .permanent { background-color: #F6E7EA; }
</style>
```

`CLASS` becomes a class unique to the plugin, so the rule cannot leak to other screens.

## Predefined classes

The `intranetcss` component provides the common design (panels, toolbars, badges, messages, listings, tabs, dark mode). Use its classes before writing new CSS: see [components](components.md).

## Global style

`public/default.css` holds what is shared. Colors that change per user or theme are CSS variables (`:root { --color: ... }`), set once in the layout.

## Static files

`/img/`, `/css/`, `/js/`, `/fonts/`, `/videos/`. Images use the file-name rule: lowercase with dashes.

## Component skins

Scope overrides to an app class combined with the official component class, for example `.forge-backtotop.ui-backtotop`. Keep the official component's selectors and behavior intact. Component CSS can be injected after the app stylesheet; use deliberate specificity instead of depending only on load order or broad global overrides.

Forge's `public/css/components.css` at commit `827311e` skins the official BackToTop this way. Preserve visible keyboard focus, sufficient contrast, mobile positioning and `prefers-reduced-motion` when adapting its appearance. Semantic or focus changes belong in a small native initialization hook, as described in [components](components.md), rather than in CSS.
